records.title: [LC] 210. Course Schedule II
records.body:
> <[210. Course Schedule II](https://leetcode.com/problems/course-schedule-ii/)> ## Approach [[Blog 정리글] directed graph의 cycle detection](https://seungriyou.github.io/posts/undirected-and-directed-graph-cycle-detection/#2-directed-graph%EC%9D%98-cycle-detection) 관련 문제
### Idea 1: Topological Sort (BFS) `indegree` 배열을 이용한 위상 정렬 문제로 풀 수 있다. 다음과 같이 directed graph와 indegree 배열을 생성한다. ```python # create graph & indegree array graph = [[] for _ in range(numCourses)] indegree = [0] * numCourses for e, s in prerequisites: graph[s].append(e) indegree[e] += 1 ``` `indegree[npos] == 0`인 원소를 deque에 넣으며 BFS로 순회한다. ```python q = deque(i for i, ind in enumerate(indegree) if ind == 0) res = [] # topological sort while q: pos = q.popleft() res.append(pos) for npos in graph[pos]: indegree[npos] -= 1 if indegree[npos] == 0: q.append(npos) ``` BFS 후, 정렬 과정에서 모은 course의 개수가 전체 course의 개수와 다르다면 전체 course를 들을 수 없는 것(= cycle이 존재)이므로 `[]`을 반환해야 함에 주의한다. ```python # if impossible to finish all courses, return empty array return res if len(res) == numCourses else [] ```
### Idea 2: 3-State DFS 다음과 같이 세 가지 상태를 가지는 DFS를 사용한다. | `visited` 값 | 의미 | | --- | --- | | `0` | 아직 방문 X | | `1` | 이미 방문 O | | `-1` | 현재 보고 있는 path에 존재 (➡️ 마주치면 **cycle** 발생) | directed graph와 DFS를 위한 `visited` 배열을 생성한다. ```python # create graph & indegree array graph = [[] for _ in range(numCourses)] visited = [False] * numCourses for e, s in prerequisites: graph[s].append(e) ``` DFS 로직의 주요 사항은 다음과 같다. - **base condition** 1. `visited[pos] == -1` 이라면, cycle이 발생한 것이므로 `False`를 반환한다. 2. `visited[pos] == 1` 이라면, 이전에 방문했던 곳이므로 더이상 해당 위치로 방문하지 않고 다음으로 넘어가기 위해 `True`를 반환한다. - **recursion** 1. 현재 `pos`를 현재 path에서 보고 있다고 표시하기 위해 `visited[pos] = -1`로 설정한다. 2. 이웃을 순회하며 `dfs(npos)`를 수행한다. 이때, 해당 결과에서 cycle이 발생했다면 `False`를 반환한다. 3. 문제 없이 이웃을 순회했다면 현재 `pos`를 방문했다고 표시하기 위해 `visited[pos] = 1`로 설정한다. - **record**: 현재 `pos`를 방문 완료했으니 `res`에 모은다. ```python res = [] def dfs(pos): # base condition # (1) cycle 발생 시 False 반환 if visited[pos] == -1: return False # (2) 이전에 방문했던 곳이라면 더이상 방문 X, True 반환 if visited[pos] == 1: return True # recur visited[pos] = -1 # 현재 pos를 보고있다고 표시 for npos in graph[pos]: # 다음 위치인 npos에서 cycle이 발생한다면 False 반환 if not dfs(npos): return False visited[pos] = 1 # 현재 pos를 방문했다고 표시 # record res.append(pos) return True ``` 모든 노드에서 `dfs()`를 수행하여 cycle이 발생하는 경우가 있다면 `[]`를 반환하고, 그게 아니라면 `res`를 뒤집어서 반환한다. (recursive 하므로 순서가 반대로 기록되게 된다) ```python for i in range(numCourses): # i에서부터 시작해서 cycle이 발생한다면 전체 course를 들을 수 없으므로 [] 반환 if not dfs(i): return [] return res[::-1] ```
## Complexity - Time: `O(N + E)` (adjacency list = `O(E)`, DFS/BFS = `O(N + E)`) - Space: `O(N + E)`

records.title: relationship loader options do a "recursive" thing inconsistently
records.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/9528

the wildcard option '*' acts recursively in some sitiuations (with no way to not be recursive) and non-recursively in others:

```py
from sqlalchemy import Column
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy import Integer
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import lazyload
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

Base = declarative_base()


class Parent(Base):
    __tablename__ = "parent"

    def __init__(self, **kw):
        kw.setdefault('children', [])
        super().__init__(**kw)

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)

    children = relationship(
        "Child",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        lazy="raise",
    )

    other_thing = relationship("OtherThing", lazy="raise")
    other_id = Column(ForeignKey('other_thing.id'))

class OtherThing(Base):
    __tablename__ = "other_thing"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


class Child(Base):
    __tablename__ = "child"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    parent_id = Column(ForeignKey("parent.id"))
    sub_children = relationship(
        "SubChild", lazy="raise", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
    )


class SubChild(Base):
    __tablename__ = "subchild"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    parent_id = Column(ForeignKey("child.id"))


e = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)
Base.metadata.create_all(e)

# fixture data
with Session(e) as sess:
    sess.add(Parent(other_thing=OtherThing(), children=[Child(sub_children=[SubChild()]), Child()]))
    sess.commit()

with Session(e) as sess:
    # is recursive ( which is surprising?)
    p1 = sess.scalars(select(Parent).options(selectinload('*'))).one()


    # works
    for c in p1.children:
        c.sub_children

with Session(e) as sess:
    # is not recursive because wildcard does not have propagate=True
    p1 = sess.scalars(select(Parent).options(lazyload('*'))).one()

    # fails
    for c in p1.children:
        c.sub_children

```

propose the best API would be:

"*" - acts one level deep only
"**" - is recursive

there's some backwards incompat here, so we'll think about the best way to do it.  however the basic idea would be:

```diff
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/path_registry.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/path_registry.py
index b117f59f78..a974b69bb0 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/path_registry.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/path_registry.py
@@ -44,6 +44,7 @@ if TYPE_CHECKING:
     from ..sql.visitors import anon_map
     from ..util.typing import _LiteralStar
     from ..util.typing import TypeGuard
+    from ..util.typing import Literal
 
     def is_root(path: PathRegistry) -> TypeGuard[RootRegistry]:
         ...
@@ -82,6 +83,7 @@ def _unreduce_path(path: _SerializedPath) -> PathRegistry:
 
 
 _WILDCARD_TOKEN: _LiteralStar = "*"
+_RECURSIVE_WILDCARD_TOKEN: Literal["**"] = "**"
 _DEFAULT_TOKEN = "_sa_default"
 
 
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
index ba4b12061a..fe7180f79b 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
@@ -35,6 +35,7 @@ from .base import InspectionAttr
 from .interfaces import LoaderOption
 from .path_registry import _DEFAULT_TOKEN
 from .path_registry import _WILDCARD_TOKEN
+from .path_registry import _RECURSIVE_WILDCARD_TOKEN
 from .path_registry import AbstractEntityRegistry
 from .path_registry import path_is_property
 from .path_registry import PathRegistry
@@ -1314,13 +1315,14 @@ class Load(_AbstractLoad):

-    __slots__ = ("strategy", "path", "local_opts")
+    __slots__ = ("strategy", "path", "local_opts", "recursive")
 
     _traverse_internals = [
         ("strategy", visitors.ExtendedInternalTraversal.dp_plain_obj),
         ("path", visitors.ExtendedInternalTraversal.dp_plain_obj),
+        ("recursive", visitors.ExtendedInternalTraversal.dp_boolean),
         (
             "local_opts",
             visitors.ExtendedInternalTraversal.dp_string_multi_dict,
@@ -1331,12 +1333,17 @@ class _WildcardLoad(_AbstractLoad):

records.title: Pruning: splice out IDENTITY neurons the IF rewrite leaves behind, recursively
records.body:
In the prune neuron logic common to Ockham and the mutation logic when a neuron becomes an IDENTITY we can often recursively remove and stay mathematically sound which will lead to a better score 

Please make sure we have this optimisation in the remove neuron logic , if not follow TDD and implement 

See https://github.com/stSoftwareAU/GRQ-sampler/commit/10b08b97bc751615f2fb7b4a6705fc5d1befaa09

<!-- GRILL-ME-UNDERSTANDING-START -->
## Current Understanding

Pruning (`prune_neuron` and `prune_synapse` in `neat-core`) can leave an `IF` hidden neuron whose condition the creature itself decides. Cleanup rewrites that `IF` into an `IDENTITY` neuron over the surviving branch (`flatten_static_if` under `IfRepair::Rewrite`) and leaves the `IDENTITY` neuron behind. Because an `IDENTITY` neuron only forwards `bias + Σ w·a`, it can be spliced out exactly by rewiring its sources straight into its targets, and one splice can make a downstream `IF` static or leave another `IDENTITY` behind, so the splice runs recursively until nothing more can go. The referenced GRQ-sampler commit shows exactly this leftover (`forest-462694b1383b3a11-if1` rewritten from `IF` to `IDENTITY` and kept). Nothing in `neat-core` performs this splice today; the TypeScript mutation path (`DiscoveryNeuronRemoval.ts` → `WasmPruneNeuron.ts`) reaches the same `prune_neuron` through WASM, so one implementation serves Ockham and mutation alike.

Facts verified in the code (default branch at `ae71f440`):

- Both prune entry points already ask cleanup for `IfRepair::Rewrite` (`prune_neuron.rs` since PR #678, `prune_synapse.rs` since Issue #591). Only `cleanup_creature`'s parity default is `IfRepair::Downgrade`, and `prune_fixtures.rs` relies on that default to reproduce the TypeScript captures. Round 3's question on moving `prune_neuron` to `Rewrite` is therefore moot: no repair-mode change is needed.
- `CleanupOptions` (`prune_cleanup.rs`) is a `Copy` + `Default` struct with one field, `if_repair`; the splice switch is a second field.
- `CleanupOutcome` already lists `removed_neurons`, `folded_neurons`, `static_if_neurons` and friends in removal order; `PruneResponse` (`prune_json.rs`) is camelCase, omits empty `Vec` fields (`skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"`) and already carries `cascadeNeurons`. The golden record is `neat-core/tests/golden/prune_wasm_parity.json`, graded by `tests/prune_json.rs`.
- `prune_neuron` runs `convert_single_edge_aggregates` before cleanup (PR #675): an aggregate the cut left with one term is already rewritten to its point-wise squash, so a single-edge aggregate target the prune itself touched will present to the splice as a summing target.
- `SquashType::is_aggregate` (`squash.rs`) and cleanup's `merge_weights` are the existing helpers for "does this target sum its terms" and "is a collision merge exact".
- Score (NEAT-AI `Score.ts` `calculateScore`, mirrored by NEAT-AI-scorer `rust_scorer/src/scoring.rs`): each hidden neuron costs `growthCost`, each synapse `growthCost / 10`, so one removed neuron pays for up to nine net new synapses. A third term charges magnitude: `100 · growthCost` times the mean over every weight and bias of `0.999 · log10|v| / 12` for `|v| > 1` (capped at twelve decades). A rewired product `w_in · w_out` has the decades of both factors, so a splice can raise this term; Round 3 accepted that this is not gated.
- The TypeScript reader (`WasmPruneShared.ts`) reads only the fields it names and ignores the rest.

### Accepted scope so far

- A new `CleanupOptions` field switches the splice on. It is off by default, so `cleanup_creature` and the `prune_fixtures` captures are byte-for-byte unchanged; both prune entry points set it on alongside `IfRepair::Rewrite`.
- Splice step in cleanup's fixed point, whole-creature sweep: every hidden `IDENTITY` neuron that qualifies is removed, whether this prune produced it, an earlier rewrite left it behind, or it pre-existed. Its bias is folded into each target's bias as `w_out · bias`, and each `(source → target)` edge is added with weight `w_in · w_out`, keeping the target-side role (`condition` / `positive` / `negative`) of the edge it replaces.
- Qualification: any bias and any inward count when every target sums its inward terms (point-wise squash, or an `IF` within one role); when a target aggregates (`is_aggregate`: `MINIMUM`, `MAXIMUM`, `MEAN`, `HYPOT`, `HYPOTv2`), only a neuron with exactly one inward edge and bias `0` is spliced, otherwise it is kept.
- A rewired edge that collides with an existing `(source → target)` edge merges by summing weights where the target sums, and the splice is refused (neuron kept) where the merge would be inexact (`MEAN`, `HYPOT`), mirroring cleanup's existing `merge_weights` rule.
- Synapse-growth rule, per splice: `edges added − edges removed ≤ 9` (strictly fewer than 10 net new synapses, after collision merges are counted), otherwise the neuron is kept. The 9 is a named constant whose doc comment cites the `Score.ts` 10:1 neuron-to-synapse ratio.
- Magnitude rule, per splice: count-only. Any finite rewired weight or folded bias is accepted; a non-finite product or bias refuses that splice (neuron kept). No comparison against the creature's current largest magnitude and no `growthCost` in the request.
- Recursion: after each pass the fixed point re-runs the `IF` rewrite, dead-structure removal, fold and splice until a pass changes nothing, so a chain of `IDENTITY` neurons and an `IF` made static by a splice collapse in the same call.
- Applies to both `prune_neuron` and `prune_synapse`; the result keeps `TransformClass::Exact` when the rest of the prune was exact, because the splice itself is exact.
- Reporting: every spliced neuron is listed by UUID on `CleanupOutcome` / `PruneResult` as `spliced_neurons`, in removal order (creature neuron order within a pass, passes in sequence), separate from `removed_neurons` / `cascadeNeurons`, and on the JSON / WASM response as `splicedNeurons`, omitted when em

records.body:
Coordination thread for three parallel cloud sessions working the tail of the
scale-validation pass (`docs/prompt-scale-validation-hitlist.md`).

**Base for all work: `claude/project-rewrite-cpp-yqutwf` @ `5cf44dfd`. Not `main`.**
Open your PR against that branch.

### Why this thread exists

The cloud sessions cannot message the coordinator directly, so this issue is
the message board. Post here rather than waiting on a reply you cannot get.

### Assignments

| session | task |
|---|---|
| A | Narrow-seam review — cache accounting, residency, invalidation, the enrichment writer, `IndexCore` shared state |
| B | Iterative builder walk — remove the CST recursion class the depth gate currently guards |
| C | `@INC` single-provider tier — the staged plan in `gold-corpus/KNOWN-GAPS.md` |

### Post a comment when

- You start, naming your task letter and the SHA you branched from.
- You hit something that changes another session's work — a shared file, a
  seam one of you is reviewing and another is editing, a design assumption
  that turns out false.
- You are blocked, or an environment limitation stops you (no `nvim`, no gold
  substrate, a proxy that blocks CPAN). Say so plainly and keep going on what
  is unblocked; a partial result with a stated gap beats a stall.
- You finish — link your PR.

### Conventions

- Prefix comments with your task letter: `[A]`, `[B]`, `[C]`.
- Report **true exit codes**. `cmd | grep` returns grep's status and will hide
  a compile failure behind a green-looking line.
- Before running gold, verify `./target/release/perl-lsp --languages` prints
  `perl, cpp (beta)`. A plain `cargo test --release` silently rebuilds
  Perl-only, after which gold skips the cpp rows and still prints green.
- Base-verify every fix: the test must FAIL before the change and pass after.
  A test that passes both ways proves nothing.
- The large corpora used earlier in this pass are local to the maintainer's
  machine and unavailable to you. Unit tests plus gold are your bar; do not
  attempt corpus-scale measurement.

Known-good baseline on `5cf44dfd`: 1,511 unit · 491 gold (0 FAIL / 0 XPASS /
0 CRASH) · e2e 113/0 · e2e-cpp 0.

records.title: research: Apache AGE & pgRouting as graph-traversal path for memory layer
records.body:
## Context

Evaluating Graphiti (getzep/graphiti) surfaced a question: do we ever need real graph-DB capabilities (multi-hop traversal, variable-length paths, Cypher-style pattern matching) on top of the planned Postgres + pgvector + relations-table memory substrate?

Current direction: **stay on Postgres + pgvector + a relations table with `start_at` / `end_at` / `source_episode_id`.** This covers 1–2 hop retrieval, which is the realistic majority of agent-memory queries. Don't pre-pay for graph traversal we're not doing yet.

This issue tracks **research** into the two middle-path options that would let us add graph-query power without adopting a separate graph DB (Neo4j/FalkorDB/Kuzu) and without the new trust boundary, backup story, or RBAC surface those drag in.

## Candidates

### Apache AGE
- Postgres extension that adds Cypher (openCypher subset) over a Postgres-backed graph.
- Same operational footprint, same backup, same RBAC, same Warden/Sentinel review surface.
- Lets us write graph traversal queries when a query genuinely needs them, without committing to a second datastore.
- Open questions: maturity vs. Postgres major versions we run, query planner behavior at depth, coexistence with pgvector in the same query, write-path performance on hot ingestion.

### pgRouting
- Postgres extension focused on graph algorithms over relational tables (shortest path, connected components, etc.).
- Lighter scope than AGE — algorithms over a normal table, not a separate graph store.
- May be the better fit if our actual need is "compute path/reachability across the relations table" rather than "express subgraph patterns."
- Open questions: which algorithms map to real memory-retrieval queries, performance on temporal edges (with `start_at`/`end_at` filters), interaction with pgvector ranking.

## Trigger conditions (revisit when any becomes true)

Don't action this issue speculatively. Revisit when:
- A real retrieval query routinely needs ≥ 3 hops and is slow because of join depth (not missing indexes).
- We find ourselves writing recursive CTEs at depth in the hot path.
- A use case appears that genuinely needs subgraph pattern matching (e.g., "find all chains of fact-supersession originating from source D").
- Source-reliability cascades through `superseded_by` chains become a hot path that recursive CTEs can't keep up with.

## Deliverable when actioned

Short comparison memo:
1. AGE vs. pgRouting vs. recursive-CTE-in-vanilla-Postgres benchmarked on one or two representative queries from the actual memory layer.
2. Trust-boundary review (extension surface, any new privileges, Warden/Sentinel implications).
3. Recommendation: adopt AGE, adopt pgRouting, stay on vanilla Postgres, or revisit later.

## Related

- Graphiti evaluation (no issue yet — surfaced in conversation 2026-05-06).
- Relations table schema (bi-temporal facts, `superseded_by`, `source_episode_id`) — to be specified.

records.title: [Feature]: Refactor Topic and Agent Session pagination, grouping, and refresh semantics
records.body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open and closed issues, and this issue consolidates the remaining refactor scope.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest `main` branch contains part of the required baseline, but does not include the remaining list, activity, invalidation, and Renderer refactor described below.

### Platform

macOS (the design and implementation are platform-agnostic)

### Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

#### Background

Topic and Agent Session surfaces currently treat DataApi cursor pagination primarily as transport batching. Page-level and legacy consumers still request or derive the complete dataset before performing search, grouping, ordering, counts, pinned composition, owner-rail selection, and local “Show more” behavior.

This creates several related problems:

- First useful render and Renderer memory usage scale with the complete Topic or Session history.
- Sidebar, right-side panel, grouped, and History consumers maintain different list derivations and refresh behavior.
- Main and Renderer can disagree about ordering, filtering, group membership, and pinned semantics.
- A committed write can leave an infinite-query cursor chain stale, causing duplicated, missing, or incorrectly ordered rows.
- Client-side filtering after pagination cannot produce reliable empty states, counts, or `hasNext` values.
- Cross-window and background-originated writes do not currently converge through an authoritative DataApi invalidation path.

#### Document contract

This issue is the **technical architecture** for the product behavior defined in #17025. It contains no product rules of its own: every user-visible behavior is referenced, never restated, and this document adds only the Topic/Session-specific contracts required to implement it. If an implementation constraint exposes a missing or conflicting product decision, resolve it in #17025 first and then update this issue. The architecture must not silently turn an implementation convenience into product behavior.

Related documents:

- #17025 — product source of truth (user-visible behavior and UX acceptance criteria).
- #17144 — generic DataApi data-change notification and bidirectional cursor infrastructure. The change-notification Phase A contract is frozen in [the architecture comment](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/17144#issuecomment-5053757668); bidirectional cursor support remains independent and open.
- #17225 — generic Renderer bidirectional collection, reconciliation, and prepend-scroll-anchoring infrastructure; its concrete API shapes remain under independent review.
- #17095 — already-landed Topic `groupId` removal and global-ordering baseline (see §2).
- #16998 — implementation PR tracking this issue.
#### Resolved product decisions

- **Search matching semantics** follow #17025 and the existing Global Search entity-matching mechanism: deferred automatic search, trimmed escaped literal-substring matching, and no additional NFC-normalization or Unicode case-folding rule introduced by this refactor. §4.5 defines the technical binding.
- **Two-pane unlinked/unknown navigation** follows #17025: the content record may open with no live owner selected and without a scoped right-side reveal. This does not change backend record eligibility.

The pseudo-owner decision is resolved: **Unlinked Assistant** and **Unknown Agent** headers are Renderer-only toggle containers, not live-owner activation targets. This is presentation policy only. Their records remain ordinary backend records and may be returned by global or pseudo-owner-scoped `/latest`, become active, and participate in any row operation the Renderer enables.

### Desired Solution

#### 1. Scope and non-goals

**In scope**: Topic/Session data and query contracts, activity-time semantics, ordering and write semantics, mapping Topic/Session writes to accepted generic change signals, surface migration, preferences, presentation state, migration, and technical verification.

**Non-goals** — this issue deliberately does not include:

- implementation or redesign of the frozen generic DataApi data-change notification protocol in #17144;
- the final generic bidirectional cursor API shape — that remains independently reviewed in #17144;
- the final generic `useInfiniteQuery`, collection-reconciliation, or prepend-scroll-anchoring API shape — those remain independently reviewed in #17225;
- entity-row push or replication between processes: SQLite remains the source of truth;
- any Topic-, Session-, Cache-, or window-specific synchronization channel;
- per-streaming-chunk or per-token database writes for activity time (§4.2);
- offline conflict resolution or multi-device synchronization;
- a global first/last move command (no product surface exists, #17025 §7);
- redesign of Assistant tag organization (#17025 §4);
- v1 list-stack fixes (v1 policy per repository guidelines).
#### 2. Current `main` baseline

PR #17095 has already landed on `main` and is baseline rather than remaining work:

- Topic `groupId`, its foreign key, schema/type/DTO/migrator usage, and response field have been removed.
- Topic manual ordering is one global `orderKey ASC, id ASC` sequence across all Assistants; Agent Session reorder already operates on one global Session sequence.
- Topic create/duplicate and Session create already insert at the first position of their global manual sequences.

This issue must not reintroduce `groupId`, repeat its migration, or treat global Topic/Session ordering as a new schema design. Baseline commit: `2481e959acbc26b0c4476d706ec02a5b189fa3e2`.

records.title: Recursive CTE over a remote/Distributed table never converges when the join to the working table is GLOBAL (`prefer_global_in_and_join = 1`): TOO_DEEP_RECURSION
records.body:
### Describe what's wrong

A finite recursive CTE (a 3-row acyclic tree that terminates at depth 2) never converges when the recursive step's join to the working table is made GLOBAL, either through `prefer_global_in_and_join = 1` or by writing `GLOBAL JOIN` explicitly. Every evaluation throws `Code: 306 ... Maximum recursive CTE evaluation depth (N) exceeded ... (TOO_DEEP_RECURSION)` for any cap (tested 4, 20 and 1000), and even when the recursive step carries an explicit bound such as `st.depth < 3`. The same query converges locally and through `remote()` without the GLOBAL rewrite.

Mechanism, from `system.query_log` of the failing run: every iteration sends the shard the same step query, `SELECT ... FROM tree AS __table1 GLOBAL ALL INNER JOIN _data_10320791693442016917_9160374414816559577 AS __table2 ON ...`. The broadcast temporary table carries the same name (hash) in every iteration and every iteration returns the same 2 rows (the depth-1 rows), so the remote never joins against the working table of the current iteration and the recursion keeps producing rows.

### Does it reproduce on the most recent release?

Yes, master `26.9.1.1437` (commit a5efd3a38a15).

### How to reproduce

```sql
CREATE TABLE tree (id String, parent_id String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id;
INSERT INTO tree VALUES ('a', ''), ('b', 'a'), ('c', 'b');

-- local: 6 (3 rows at depth 0, 2 at depth 1, 1 at depth 2)
WITH RECURSIVE st AS (
    SELECT id, parent_id, toUInt64(0) AS depth FROM tree
    UNION ALL
    SELECT t.id, t.parent_id, depth + 1 FROM tree AS t, st WHERE t.parent_id = st.id)
SELECT count() FROM st;

-- remote() without GLOBAL: 6
WITH RECURSIVE st AS (
    SELECT id, parent_id, toUInt64(0) AS depth FROM remote('127.0.0.1', currentDatabase(), tree)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT t.id, t.parent_id, depth + 1 FROM remote('127.0.0.1', currentDatabase(), tree) AS t, st WHERE t.parent_id = st.id)
SELECT count() FROM st;

-- the same query with the join to the working table made GLOBAL: never converges
WITH RECURSIVE st AS (
    SELECT id, parent_id, toUInt64(0) AS depth FROM remote('127.0.0.1', currentDatabase(), tree)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT t.id, t.parent_id, depth + 1 FROM remote('127.0.0.1', currentDatabase(), tree) AS t, st WHERE t.parent_id = st.id)
SELECT count() FROM st
SETTINGS prefer_global_in_and_join = 1, max_recursive_cte_evaluation_depth = 20;

-- an explicitly bounded recursive step with an explicit GLOBAL JOIN does not terminate either
WITH RECURSIVE st AS (
    SELECT id, parent_id, toUInt64(0) AS depth FROM remote('127.0.0.1', currentDatabase(), tree)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT t.id, t.parent_id, depth + 1 FROM remote('127.0.0.1', currentDatabase(), tree) AS t GLOBAL JOIN st ON t.parent_id = st.id AND st.depth < 3)
SELECT count() FROM st
SETTINGS max_recursive_cte_evaluation_depth = 20;
```

Result of the last two queries:

```
Code: 306. DB::Exception: Maximum recursive CTE evaluation depth (20) exceeded, during evaluation of  st. Consider raising max_recursive_cte_evaluation_depth setting: While executing RecursiveCTESource. (TOO_DEEP_RECURSION)
```

The same happens with a `Distributed` table in place of `remote()` (with `prefer_localhost_replica = 0` or `1`). `distributed_product_mode = 'global'` alone does not trigger it (the join partner is a CTE, not a Distributed table, so nothing is rewritten). Deterministic, 5/5.

### Expected behavior

`6`, as without the GLOBAL rewrite — the recursion terminates after two steps.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114012
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115799
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/90838

Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

records.title: integration(context-fabric): bind batch lifecycle evidence to a released Context Assertion contract
records.body:
## Buyer / integration gap

`pg-llm-batch` owns durable/asynchronous PostgreSQL batch preparation, token/size accounting, tenant/RLS state, provider-neutral batch lifecycle ports, lifecycle/reconciliation/result ingestion, audit/provenance, recovery evidence, and the local transactional lifecycle outbox. `contextual-orchestrator` owns model/provider discovery, routing/fallback, and credentials.

Production Context Fabric integration may consume only an immutable released `context-graph-contracts` contract through a pg-owned anti-corruption layer. Mutable PR heads/branches are candidate/test evidence only; no sibling source copy, cross-service SQL, prompt/response/provider-body replication, or enterprise-architecture authority promotion is allowed.

## Authority and evidence discipline

This issue is a durable integration contract, not a hand-maintained snapshot of current branch heads, workflow run IDs, review state, release inventory, or central `.github` topology. Before any mutation or production-adoption decision, re-read protected/default refs, relevant owner PRs, exact heads/bases, checks, reviews/threads, release inventory, and branch overlap from their live owners. `pg-llm-batch#244` is the mutable cross-repository integration ledger for those observations.

Workflow success is not approval. A mutable exact-head GREEN is not protected integration or immutable release authority. Source/base movement invalidates predecessor acceptance evidence. Descendants reconcile only through ordinary/non-force ancestry after foundations land.

The live organization governance contract must also be read rather than inferred from historical PR state. Central `.github#772` owns the solo-maintainer approval-policy defect; deterministic workflow/security/SAST/thread/branch-integrity gates must remain enforced, and self-approval, fabricated reviewers, routine administrator bypass, or bot/model review represented as human approval are not acceptable substitutes.

## Runtime column authority — real PostgreSQL REDs -> causal repairs -> exact-head GREEN

Migration 0009 already re-proved the final 14-column catalog identity at migration verification, but continuing `_require_rls_application_role()` did not initially re-prove the complete column contract before lifecycle outbox I/O.

Historical RED `7ba53c79b50f0f1d204f0f282927a71ec95bb301` drops `NOT NULL` from `evidence_id`, proves two NULL replay identities can coexist under the surviving CHECK/UNIQUE program, and requires an ordinary `NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS` application role to fail continuing runtime admission before tenant binding/data I/O. It rejects missing/additional/dropped columns, type/collation/nullability/default-presence drift, and generated/identity authority before tenant binding or outbox data I/O. Historical RED `c3916340284950a42b31abc6f39a8d275b003200`, CI `34193807153`, isolates a same-type modifier drift: canonical unrestricted `created_at timestamptz` is changed only to `timestamp(0) with time zone`; live `atttypid`, collation, `NOT NULL`, default presence/expression, generated and identity state remain canonical while `atttypmod` and stored fractional-second semantics change. Migration/runtime admission still accepted it (`runtime_rejected=0 migration_rejected=0`). Release Acceptance `34193807165` independently succeeds.

Minimum repair `2dd8e10def93b18e8973a99a897b8625763a9e7c` adds reviewed canonical `pg_attribute.atttypmod = -1` identity for all 14 columns to continuing runtime admission, migration 0009, and the byte-identical Docker initializer. A later child updates the stale static test contract to require the typmod predicate without weakening production semantics.

The valid CodeRabbit typmod finding was repaired. Its separate suggestion to bind tenant scope before live authority admission was verified against `AGENTS.md` and current code and rejected: tenant-scope value validation precedes database I/O, while the database path retains relation lock -> live authority admission -> parameterized transaction-local `set_config` -> row I/O. The retained admission boundary includes exact CHECK/default dependency identity; forced-RLS policy identity; selectable/administerable session-role authority; recursive mixed `SET`/`ADMIN` delegation; caller-visible `SECURITY DEFINER` and `SECURITY INVOKER` tenant-setting authority; routine `search_path`; ordinary-view effective-principal closure; materialized-copy provenance; direct/view/definer/delegated foreign-data authority; inheritance/partition parents with foreign descendants; table-program/index authority; same-consuming-statement admitted-OID/name proofs; relation storage/topology identity; complete column identity; and the read/write retained-lock fence.

Any current implementation descendants that carry these repairs remain candidate evidence until they are normally integrated and their final exact head re-acquires all then-live checks/reviews. Do not transfer historical GREEN receipts onto a moved descendant.
